name: Planning & Setting SAE Goals

objectives.text: Identify personal interests in plants, animals, food, or the outdoors that could become a simple agricultural project
List the steps involved in starting a simple agricultural project at home or school
Distinguish between short-term and long-term goals for an agricultural project
Describe how setting goals gives direction to an SAE project and helps measure success
Identify the resources an SAE project requires, including time, money, space, equipment, and adult help
Write SAE goals that are specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-bound
Create a timeline of tasks and milestones that leads to completing an SAE goal
Explain what Supervised Agricultural Experience is and why careful planning makes an SAE a valuable work-based learning experience
Analyze how SAE goals can connect personal interests to an AFNR career pathway and develop lifelong career skills
Assess personal resources and constraints to determine whether a proposed SAE is feasible
Identify the information needed to complete an SAE plan, including SMART goals, a needs assessment, and a projected budget
Apply goal-setting steps to draft a one-year SAE plan with goals, action steps, and a timeline
Design a safety plan that identifies hazards and safe practices for a planned SAE
Develop a training agreement that defines the responsibilities of the student, parent or guardian, employer, and agriculture teacher in an SAE
Develop a written SAE plan with goals, a projected budget, and a method for tracking progress and defend its feasibility
Develop a multi-year SAE growth plan aligned with FFA degree and proficiency award requirements
Develop production goals for a plant-based SAE that account for environmental factors
Evaluate input from the agriculture teacher, parents, and employers to improve an SAE plan
Evaluate progress toward SAE goals and revise goals in response to changing circumstances
Justify how SAE goals prepare a student for post-secondary education and a future AFNR career

changes: Kept and reworded all six existing objectives, made the grade 8 one a SMART goal writing competency, changed the grade 11 plan to track progress instead of building a record-keeping system to avoid overlapping the record keeping sibling, and made grade 12 revision an evaluation objective. Added interest identification, short- versus long-term goals, resource identification, timelines, the value of SAE planning, career pathway alignment, feasibility assessment, plan components, safety planning, training agreements, multi-year growth tied to FFA degrees and proficiencies, plant production goals, stakeholder input, and post-secondary justification. Tagged AFNR standards only on grade 9 to 12 objectives where they fit.
